claude.country: Ghana, Netherlands, Germany, UK (RODAM); South Africa; Sweden
claude.sample_unit: participants across three prospective cohorts (1607 RODAM-Pros, 515 MASC, 3044 VIP)
models_evaluated: Epidemiological Study on the Insulin Resistance Syndrome (DESIR) model

links.outcome: Calibration error before and after local recalibration of diabetes risk models
links.effect: Most models substantially underestimated risk; recalibration eliminated systematic miscalibration and reduced calibration error to ≤2.3% in RODAM-Pros and VIP and ≤3.4% in MASC.
links.quote: Recalibration eliminated systematic miscalibration and reduced calibration error to ≤ 2.3% in RODAM-Pros and VIP and ≤ 3.4% in MASC.

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of externally evaluated models in new populations
links.effect: All models had poor-to-modest discrimination (c-statistic <0.7); most models substantially underestimated risk before recalibration.

models_evaluated: Epidemiological Study on the Insulin Resistance Syndrome model

links.effect: Recalibration eliminated systematic miscalibration and reduced calibration error to ≤ 2.3% in RODAM-Pros and VIP and ≤ 3.4% in MASC.
links.quote: Recalibration eliminated systematic miscalibration and reduced calibration error to ≤ 2.3% in RODAM-Pros and VIP and ≤ 3.4% in MASC.

links.effect: Performance varied by sex and cohort.
links.quote: Performance varied by sex and cohort.

links.effect: Existing diabetes risk models were applicable only after recalibration to local risk levels.
links.quote: Existing diabetes risk prediction models can be applied to predict incident dysglycaemia in both Sub-Saharan African and European populations, but only after recalibration to local risk levels.
